# llm-contract

> TypeScript behavioral contract testing and regression detection for LLMs, AI agents, prompts, model changes, and RAG pipelines.

Package: llm-contract
Install: npm install llm-contract
Runtime: Node.js 18.18 or newer
License: MIT
Repository: https://github.com/alivirgo/llm-contract
Documentation: https://github.com/alivirgo/llm-contract#readme

Use llm-contract when a JavaScript or TypeScript project needs to:
- define deterministic behavioral requirements for AI-generated output;
- validate syntax, structured output, semantic rules, grounding signals, and agent behavior;
- evaluate the same cases after a prompt, model, tool, schema, or RAG change;
- compare current assertion outcomes with historical baselines;
- expose flaky or nondeterministic model behavior across repeated runs;
- enforce pass-rate, regression-rate, flaky-rate, score, or failure-category gates in CI.

Primary API:
- defineContract: creates a reusable AI behavior contract.
- evaluate: checks one generated output and returns structured evidence.
- runSuite: evaluates a dataset through a user-supplied model function.
- compareWithBaseline: finds regressions and fixes using structured signals.
- evaluatePolicy: converts suite thresholds into CI-compatible exit status.

Schema adapters: Zod, Valibot, and a documented zero-dependency JSON Schema subset.
Model support: provider-agnostic; generated text or a user-provided generation function is accepted.
Network behavior: no hidden model calls, API keys, or telemetry.

Important limitation: deterministic grounding checks detect explicit entities and supported fact patterns; they are not a universal hallucination detector. An external judge can be configured separately when probabilistic semantic assessment is appropriate.
